cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Traffic-control devices include _____ that regulate road traffic.
cards.back: Traffic-control devices include signs, signals and pavement markings that regulate road traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A driver must recognize traffic controls promptly and obey _____ signs.
cards.back: A driver must recognize traffic controls promptly and obey regulatory signs.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Traffic directions given by law-_____ officers, highway personnel and school crossing guards must be obeyed.
cards.back: Traffic directions given by law-enforcement officers, highway personnel and school crossing guards must be obeyed.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A sign’s shape can indicate its meaning _____ the driver can read its message.
cards.back: A sign’s shape can indicate its meaning before the driver can read its message.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Recognizing a sign’s color and shape helps a driver adjust speed and driving behavior _____ reading its words.
cards.back: Recognizing a sign’s color and shape helps a driver adjust speed and driving behavior before reading its words.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The _____ is reserved for stop signs, which require slowing and making a full stop.
cards.back: The octagon is reserved for stop signs, which require slowing and making a full stop.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Rectangular _____ signs can address speed, school zones, parking or loading.
cards.back: Rectangular regulatory signs can address speed, school zones, parking or loading.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A _____ -shaped sign warns of a hazard or approaching condition.
cards.back: A diamond-shaped sign warns of a hazard or approaching condition.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: An _____ diamond warns of a construction zone and calls for slower, cautious travel.
cards.back: An orange diamond warns of a construction zone and calls for slower, cautious travel.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Yellow _____ can warn of curves, side roads or changes in traffic flow.
cards.back: Yellow diamonds can warn of curves, side roads or changes in traffic flow.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A downward-pointing _____ is reserved for yield signs; slow, observe approaching traffic and be ready to stop when necessary.
cards.back: A downward-pointing triangle is reserved for yield signs; slow, observe approaching traffic and be ready to stop when necessary.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A sideways-pointing _____ sign marks a no-passing zone.
cards.back: A sideways-pointing triangular sign marks a no-passing zone.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A white railroad crossbuck is a _____ sign with the meaning of a yield sign.
cards.back: A white railroad crossbuck is a regulatory sign with the meaning of a yield sign.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A horizontal rectangle can be used for guidance, some _____ or temporary traffic control.
cards.back: A horizontal rectangle can be used for guidance, some warnings or temporary traffic control.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Route markers can use shapes other than the main stop, yield, warning and _____ shapes.
cards.back: Route markers can use shapes other than the main stop, yield, warning and regulatory shapes.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ on a stop, yield, do-not-enter or wrong-way sign communicates stopping or a prohibited action.
cards.back: Red on a stop, yield, do-not-enter or wrong-way sign communicates stopping or a prohibited action.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ is a temporary-control background color that warns of construction.
cards.back: Orange is a temporary-control background color that warns of construction.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ warning or school-sign backgrounds call for caution, alertness and readiness to slow.
cards.back: Amber warning or school-sign backgrounds call for caution, alertness and readiness to slow.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Black can be the background for _____ -way, night-speed-limit and truck-regulation signs.
cards.back: Black can be the background for one-way, night-speed-limit and truck-regulation signs.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Black lettering can appear on white, yellow, orange, fluorescent-_____ or fluorescent-yellow-green sign backgrounds.
cards.back: Black lettering can appear on white, yellow, orange, fluorescent-pink or fluorescent-yellow-green sign backgrounds.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: White is used behind most _____ signs and some route markers.
cards.back: White is used behind most regulatory signs and some route markers.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: White lettering can appear on red, green, blue, _____ or black sign backgrounds.
cards.back: White lettering can appear on red, green, blue, brown or black sign backgrounds.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Blue can identify traveler services, information, _____ routes and portions of some route markers.
cards.back: Blue can identify traveler services, information, evacuation routes and portions of some route markers.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Light _____ is used for disability-parking signs.
cards.back: Light blue is used for disability-parking signs.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ backgrounds provide guidance or information, while green wording can indicate permissive regulation or parking.
cards.back: Green backgrounds provide guidance or information, while green wording can indicate permissive regulation or parking.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Fluorescent yellow-green backgrounds identify pedestrian, bicycle and school _____ .
cards.back: Fluorescent yellow-green backgrounds identify pedestrian, bicycle and school warnings.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ backgrounds identify guidance for recreational or cultural destinations.
cards.back: Brown backgrounds identify guidance for recreational or cultural destinations.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Fluorescent _____ backgrounds identify incident-management signs, such as storm-related controls or a crash closure.
cards.back: Fluorescent pink backgrounds identify incident-management signs, such as storm-related controls or a crash closure.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Warning signs alert a driver to possible danger, a hazard or a special roadway situation _____ .
cards.back: Warning signs alert a driver to possible danger, a hazard or a special roadway situation ahead.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A warning may _____ slowing and being ready to stop.
cards.back: A warning may require slowing and being ready to stop.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Warning signs are usually yellow _____ with black lettering or symbols.
cards.back: Warning signs are usually yellow diamonds with black lettering or symbols.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Some school-zone, school-crossing and pedestrian-crossing _____ use fluorescent yellow.
cards.back: Some school-zone, school-crossing and pedestrian-crossing warnings use fluorescent yellow.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ signs communicate laws governing traffic direction, lane use, turns, speed, parking or another special situation.
cards.back: Regulatory signs communicate laws governing traffic direction, lane use, turns, speed, parking or another special situation.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A _____ circle and red slash over a symbol prohibit the depicted action.
cards.back: A red circle and red slash over a symbol prohibit the depicted action.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A speed-limit sign may specify the maximum legal speed or a _____ minimum speed.
cards.back: A speed-limit sign may specify the maximum legal speed or a required minimum speed.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A posted _____ is appropriate only for ideal conditions, and weather, traffic or limited visibility can require a lower speed.
cards.back: A posted maximum is appropriate only for ideal conditions, and weather, traffic or limited visibility can require a lower speed.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The school-zone speed on a School Speed Limit When Flashing sign applies while the lights _____ ; otherwise the ordinary roadway limit applies.
cards.back: The school-zone speed on a School Speed Limit When Flashing sign applies while the lights flash; otherwise the ordinary roadway limit applies.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Lane-use signs identify permitted travel or turning movements and may stand _____ the road or hang over a lane.
cards.back: Lane-use signs identify permitted travel or turning movements and may stand beside the road or hang over a lane.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ painted on the pavement can supplement lane-use signs.
cards.back: Arrows painted on the pavement can supplement lane-use signs.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A stop sign is _____ -sided, red and lettered in white.
cards.back: A stop sign is eight-sided, red and lettered in white.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: At a stop sign, stop _____ a provided stop line or crosswalk.
cards.back: At a stop sign, stop behind a provided stop line or crosswalk.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: After stopping, check all directions and yield to crossing vehicles and pedestrians before entering when _____ .
cards.back: After stopping, check all directions and yield to crossing vehicles and pedestrians before entering when safe.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: An all-way or numbered-way plaque at a stop-controlled intersection indicates that every approaching _____ has a stop sign.
cards.back: An all-way or numbered-way plaque at a stop-controlled intersection indicates that every approaching direction has a stop sign.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A yield sign is a red-and-white triangle pointed downward and requires allowing traffic with the _____ of way to proceed first.
cards.back: A yield sign is a red-and-white triangle pointed downward and requires allowing traffic with the right of way to proceed first.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A shared center left-turn lane serves left turns from either _____ and cannot be used for through travel or passing.
cards.back: A shared center left-turn lane serves left turns from either direction and cannot be used for through travel or passing.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: When making a left turn from the shared center lane, a driver must not travel more than _____ feet within that lane.
cards.back: When making a left turn from the shared center lane, a driver must not travel more than two hundred feet within that lane.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A No Turn on Red sign forbids a right turn during the red phase, so the driver must _____ for green.
cards.back: A No Turn on Red sign forbids a right turn during the red phase, so the driver must wait for green.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Stop Here on _____ sign identifies the stopping location for a red signal.
cards.back: A Stop Here on Red sign identifies the stopping location for a red signal.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Without a No Turn on Red prohibition, a right turn on red is _____ after stopping at the line and checking traffic and pedestrians.
cards.back: Without a No Turn on Red prohibition, a right turn on red is permitted after stopping at the line and checking traffic and pedestrians.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Do _____ Block Intersection sign prohibits stopping, standing or parking in the intersection.
cards.back: A Do Not Block Intersection sign prohibits stopping, standing or parking in the intersection.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do _____ enter an intersection when traffic prevents clearing it completely.
cards.back: Do not enter an intersection when traffic prevents clearing it completely.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A _____ Turn Yield on Green sign permits a left turn only after yielding to approaching traffic.
cards.back: A Left Turn Yield on Green sign permits a left turn only after yielding to approaching traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: On a _____ -way street, traffic must follow the sign’s arrow rather than travel in the opposite direction.
cards.back: On a one-way street, traffic must follow the sign’s arrow rather than travel in the opposite direction.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Do _____ Pass sign marks a location where passing another vehicle is forbidden.
cards.back: A Do Not Pass sign marks a location where passing another vehicle is forbidden.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Passing-zone decisions account for _____ and hidden hazards such as curves, hills, intersections or entry points.
cards.back: Passing-zone decisions account for sight distance and hidden hazards such as curves, hills, intersections or entry points.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Pass with Care sign ends a no-passing zone but permits passing only when _____ .
cards.back: A Pass with Care sign ends a no-passing zone but permits passing only when safe.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Keep Right sign directs traffic to the right of a feature such as a _____ , island or obstruction.
cards.back: A Keep Right sign directs traffic to the right of a feature such as a median, island or obstruction.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: On a multilane highway, Slower Traffic Keep Right directs vehicles below the normal _____ to the right lane.
cards.back: On a multilane highway, Slower Traffic Keep Right directs vehicles below the normal traffic speed to the right lane.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The Do Not Enter design has a _____ horizontal bar inside a red circle and prohibits entering the roadway opening.
cards.back: The Do Not Enter design has a white horizontal bar inside a red circle and prohibits entering the roadway opening.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Wrong Way sign indicates that the vehicle is already traveling against the _____ direction.
cards.back: A Wrong Way sign indicates that the vehicle is already traveling against the permitted direction.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Wrong Way signs may appear beyond a Do Not Enter sign on a ramp or after an incorrect turn onto a _____ -way street, alley or driveway.
cards.back: Wrong Way signs may appear beyond a Do Not Enter sign on a ramp or after an incorrect turn onto a one-way street, alley or driveway.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A highway-evacuation sign identifies a route _____ for emergency evacuation.
cards.back: A highway-evacuation sign identifies a route designated for emergency evacuation.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A railroad crossbuck is _____ at public rail crossings and requires yielding to a train.
cards.back: A railroad crossbuck is required at public rail crossings and requires yielding to a train.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Guide signs provide road, destination, point-of-interest or service information and may be green, _____ or blue.
cards.back: Guide signs provide road, destination, point-of-interest or service information and may be green, brown or blue.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ signs show directions or distances to places such as cities, airports and jurisdiction boundaries.
cards.back: Destination signs show directions or distances to places such as cities, airports and jurisdiction boundaries.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The side of an _____ sign on which the word Exit appears indicates whether the exit lane or ramp is on the left or right.
cards.back: The side of an exit sign on which the word Exit appears indicates whether the exit lane or ramp is on the left or right.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A left-_____ sign may use yellow to draw additional attention.
cards.back: A left-exit sign may use yellow to draw additional attention.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Blue service signs with _____ letters or symbols identify amenities such as rest areas, fuel, lodging or hospitals.
cards.back: Blue service signs with white letters or symbols identify amenities such as rest areas, fuel, lodging or hospitals.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The shape and color of a route-number marker indicate the roadway _____ .
cards.back: The shape and color of a route-number marker indicate the roadway category.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Use a map or navigation system to _____ a route and follow its route markers while traveling through unfamiliar areas.
cards.back: Use a map or navigation system to plan a route and follow its route markers while traveling through unfamiliar areas.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Temporary incident signs warn of needed stops, closures or _____ caused by unplanned events such as a crash, natural disaster or hazardous spill.
cards.back: Temporary incident signs warn of needed stops, closures or detours caused by unplanned events such as a crash, natural disaster or hazardous spill.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Incident signs use fluorescent _____ backgrounds with black lettering.
cards.back: Incident signs use fluorescent pink backgrounds with black lettering.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide connects roadside-incident warnings with Louisiana’s _____ requirements.
cards.back: The guide connects roadside-incident warnings with Louisiana’s move-over requirements.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Orange work-area _____ indicate nearby workers, machinery or barriers and may require slowing, stopping or changing lanes.
cards.back: Orange work-area warnings indicate nearby workers, machinery or barriers and may require slowing, stopping or changing lanes.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Work-zone traffic controls can include signs, _____ , drums, cones, tubes, arrow panels and flag persons.
cards.back: Work-zone traffic controls can include signs, barricades, drums, cones, tubes, arrow panels and flag persons.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ is the basic color for construction and maintenance traffic-control devices.
cards.back: Orange is the basic color for construction and maintenance traffic-control devices.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Most work-area warning signs are _____ , although some are rectangles.
cards.back: Most work-area warning signs are diamonds, although some are rectangles.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Flagger _____ warning calls for slowing and being prepared to stop for the flag person.
cards.back: A Flagger Ahead warning calls for slowing and being prepared to stop for the flag person.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Workers _____ warning calls for reduced speed and a lane position farther from workers.
cards.back: A Workers Ahead warning calls for reduced speed and a lane position farther from workers.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A Low Shoulder warning identifies a _____ at the pavement edge; if leaving the pavement, slow and steer firmly.
cards.back: A Low Shoulder warning identifies a sharp drop at the pavement edge; if leaving the pavement, slow and steer firmly.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ speed in a work zone and remain prepared to stop.
cards.back: Reduce speed in a work zone and remain prepared to stop.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Reduced work-zone speed limits _____ both road users and workers.
cards.back: Reduced work-zone speed limits protect both road users and workers.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide states that Louisiana construction-zone traffic fines are _____ .
cards.back: The guide states that Louisiana construction-zone traffic fines are doubled.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Work-zone lane shifts or alternating closures may change daily, so familiar long-term work areas still _____ attention.
cards.back: Work-zone lane shifts or alternating closures may change daily, so familiar long-term work areas still require attention.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ , vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes warn of unusual work-area conditions and guide traffic through the zone.
cards.back: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes warn of unusual work-area conditions and guide traffic through the zone.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: At _____ , work-area channelizing devices may carry flashing or steady lights.
cards.back: At night, work-area channelizing devices may carry flashing or steady lights.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Diagonal barricade stripes sloping down to the _____ direct traffic to pass on the left.
cards.back: Diagonal barricade stripes sloping down to the left direct traffic to pass on the left.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Diagonal barricade stripes sloping down to the _____ direct traffic to pass on the right.
cards.back: Diagonal barricade stripes sloping down to the right direct traffic to pass on the right.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Flashing or sequential arrow panels can guide vehicles into particular lanes and warn of a road or street _____ during either daylight or darkness.
cards.back: Flashing or sequential arrow panels can guide vehicles into particular lanes and warn of a road or street closure during either daylight or darkness.
